summary: Constance Kassor works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She earned a BA from Smith College and a PhD from Emory University under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, also studying with Jay L. Garfield and Ngawang Jorden, and joined Smith's faculty.
Constance Powell Chin works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She earned a Master's degree at San Jose State University by 2012 and studied under Christian Luczanits.

Constantin Régamey (1907–1982) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. He studied at the Universities of Warsaw and Paris under Stanisław Schayer, Jean Przyluski, Marcelle Lalou, and Józef Turczyński, later teaching at Warsaw, Fribourg, and Lausanne.

Cornelis Christiaan Berg (1900–1990) was a linguist who studied at Leiden University (~1919–1927). He held posts at Leiden University (1929–1971) and the University of Amsterdam (1950–1967), and taught Jan Gonda.

Cornelis Jan Kuiken works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under MA supervisor Jaap den Hollander and earned his PhD at the University of Groningen by 2002 under doctoral supervisors Timothy H. Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) studied at the University of Amsterdam and Remonstrant Seminary. A religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian scholar, he held posts at Rotterdam, Remonstrant Seminary, Leiden University (1877–1901), and the University of Edinburgh.

Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Raniero Gnoli. He served as Professor of Religions and Philosophy of India and the Far East at Sapienza University of Rome.

Craig Jamieson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at the University of Cambridge, serving as curator for the South Asia manuscript collection around 2012, and was a fellow at Queens' College, Cambridge.
Craig Preston is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Cristina Pecchia works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (PhD ~1999–2003) and the University of Vienna, under Raniero Gnoli, Raffaele Torella, Corrado Pensa, and Ernst Steinkellner, later researching at IKGA.

Csaba Dezső (b. 1973) is an Indologist who earned master's degrees from Eötvös Loránd University and a PhD from the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1998–2004). He became an Assistant Lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University around 2003.

Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held posts as a research assistant at Eötvös Loránd University and at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024).

Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She held positions as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Culadasa (1944–2021) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. He studied under Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu, taught Matthew Immergut, and served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011).
Cuma Ozkan works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD from Indiana University under John R. McRae, later serving as an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel is a scholar of Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Keizaburo Mizuno and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2009).
Cynthia Col is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.
Cynthia M. Beall (b. 1949) is a scholar in Tibetology and related fields. She studied at Pennsylvania State University (~1971–1976) and took up a post at Case Western Reserve University in 1976.
